title: कृत्प्रत्ययः — The Primary (Verbal Root) Derivative Affix Rule Book
subtitle: The standard, commonly-taught set of कृत्-प्रत्ययs (affixes attaching directly to a verbal root to form participles, infinitives, gerunds, and agent/action nouns)
source_note: IMPORTANT PROVENANCE NOTE, DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER FILES IN THIS PROJECT: the user's own authoritative source for this batch -- Dr. Ghanashyam Dora's English translation of the Laghusiddhāntakaumudī -- was checked directly (table of contents, page by page) and does NOT include a kṛt-pratyaya chapter; that translated volume's scope is explicitly limited to Saṃjñā, Paribhāṣā, Sandhi, Kāraka, Samāsa, and Strī-pratyaya only (kṛt-pratyaya appears later in the full Siddhāntakaumudī tradition, in a volume/section not covered by this particular translation). This file is therefore built from general, well-established Pāṇinian grammar knowledge (the same 14-affix set commonly taught in Sanskrit pedagogy and cited across standard grammar references), NOT independently re-verified page-by-page against a critical edition the way the strī-pratyaya file was. Sūtra numbers given are the well-known, standard citations for these affixes; confidence should be treated as lower than the PDF-sourced files in this project, and flagged as such throughout.

how_to_read.ashtadhyayi_ref: Chapter.Pada.Sutra number in Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī (standard citation, not re-verified this session)
how_to_read.krdanta: कृदन्तः -- a word formed by kṛt-suffixation of a verbal root
how_to_read.process: what kind of word the affix forms (participle/infinitive/gerund/agent-noun/action-noun) and its declension behavior

avyaya_krt.english_name: ktvā: gerund/absolutive ('having done X'), for a simple (non-prefixed) root
avyaya_krt.rule: Added to a root to form an indeclinable (अव्यय) gerund meaning 'having done [the root's action]', used when the SAME agent performs two successive actions -- the action in क्त्वा-form happens first. Used only when the root has no verbal prefix (उपसर्ग); with a prefix, ल्यप् (krt-2) is used instead.
related_ashtadhyayi: 7.1.37 (governs the ktvā/lyap split by presence of a prefix)
avyaya_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

examples.gloss: 'having read' -- सः पठित्वा अत्र आगमिष्यति ('he will come here after reading')

avyaya_krt.english_name: lyap: gerund/absolutive, for a root WITH a verbal prefix (replaces क्त्वा)
avyaya_krt.rule: The same 'having done X' gerund sense as क्त्वा, but used specifically when the root carries a verbal prefix (उपसर्ग) -- ल्यप् replaces क्त्वा in that context, surfacing as -य after the (usually sandhi-modified) root.
avyaya_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

avyaya_krt.english_name: tumun: infinitive ('in order to do X' / 'to do X')
avyaya_krt.rule: Added to a root to form an indeclinable infinitive, used when one agent's action is undertaken FOR THE PURPOSE of another action -- comparable to English 'to X' / 'in order to X'.
avyaya_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

examples.gloss: 'to go' -- बालकः गृहं गन्तुम् उद्यतः अस्ति ('the boy is ready to go home')

adjectival_krt.english_name: śatṛ: present active participle (परस्मैपदी), '[one who is] doing X'
adjectival_krt.rule: Added to a परस्मैपदी present-tense stem to form an adjectival present participle, declining like a t-stem (with an inserted nasal for thematic stems, e.g. -अन्त्-/-न्त्-). Used for the परस्मैपद side; शानच् (krt-5) is the corresponding आत्मनेपद affix.
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

adjectival_krt.english_name: śānac: present middle participle (आत्मनेपदी), '[one who is] doing X (for oneself)'
adjectival_krt.rule: The आत्मनेपद counterpart of शतृ (krt-4): added to an आत्मनेपदी present-tense stem to form the corresponding present participle.
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

adjectival_krt.english_name: kta: past passive participle, '[having been] done'
adjectival_krt.rule: Added to a root to form the past passive participle, meaning '[that which has been] X-ed'. Grouped together with क्तवतु (krt-7) under the technical term निष्ठा.
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

adjectival_krt.english_name: ktavatu: past active participle (agent sense), '[one who] has done X'
adjectival_krt.rule: Grouped with क्त (krt-6) under निष्ठा, but expresses the ACTIVE/agent sense ('one who has done X') rather than the passive sense -- declines with the possessive-suffix pattern (nominative -वान्).
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

adjectival_krt.english_name: tavyat and anīyar: gerundive/obligative, '[X] must/should be done'
adjectival_krt.rule: Both affixes independently express the same gerundive (potential passive) sense -- 'ought to be/must be done' -- and are largely interchangeable, forming an adjective agreeing with the (grammatical) object.
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

examples.gloss: तेन संस्कृतं पठितव्यम् ('he should study Sanskrit')

adjectival_krt.english_name: yat, ṇyat, kyap: a further set of gerundive-forming affixes (root-specific alternatives to tavyat/anIyar)
adjectival_krt.rule: Three further affixes carrying the same basic gerundive ('ought to be done') sense as तव्यत्/अनीयर् (krt-8), each attaching to different, largely root-specific subsets of verbs rather than being freely interchangeable.
adjectival_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

examples.gloss: 'verse' (lit. 'that which is to be gone through/composed')

nominal_krt.english_name: tṛc: agent noun, '[one who] does X (habitually/characteristically)'
nominal_krt.rule: Added to a root to form an r-stem agent-noun meaning 'a doer of X' -- productive and very common, declining like the ऋ-stem nouns पितृ/भ्रातृ.
nominal_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

nominal_krt.english_name: ṇvul and lyuṭ: further agent/action-noun affixes (surfacing as -अक and -अन)
nominal_krt.rule: ण्वुल् (surfacing as -अक) forms an agent noun like तृच् but declining as a regular अ-stem; ल्युट् (surfacing as -अन) forms an ACTION noun ('the act of X-ing') rather than an agent noun.
nominal_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

examples.gloss: 'a maker, an agent/causer' (also the technical grammar term for a semantic role)

nominal_krt.english_name: ktin: feminine abstract action noun, 'the act/state of X-ing'
nominal_krt.rule: Added to a root to form a feminine i-stem abstract noun denoting the action itself -- comparable to English '-tion'/'-ing' as an abstract noun (गति, स्थिति, बुद्धि etc.).
nominal_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

nominal_krt.english_name: ṇini: agent noun with a habitual/characteristic sense, '[one who] habitually does X'
nominal_krt.rule: Forms an in-stem agent noun (nominative -ई) with a stronger habitual/characterizing sense than तृच् -- 'one who characteristically/professionally does X'.
nominal_krt.book_ref: general Paninian grammar reference, not from the user's LSK source (see source_note)

summary_counts.status: Covers the standard 13-14 affix set commonly taught as an introductory kṛt-pratyaya survey: 3 indeclinable-forming (ktvā/lyap/tumun), 6 participle/gerundive-forming, and 4 noun-forming affixes. This is a representative pedagogical subset -- the Aṣṭādhyāyī's actual kṛt section (roughly 3.1 through 3.4) defines several hundred kṛt affixes in total; exhaustive coverage was not attempted.
